title: Design a URL Shortener
answer: At 10 billion redirects a month, plan for about 3,850 average and 19,000 peak redirects per second. Generate random short codes with a Postgres primary key and collision retries, serve redirects through a CDN/cache, and count clicks asynchronously. Short TTLs plus purges make takedowns fast.
focus: Estimate a read-heavy workload, then decide what to cache and how to count clicks without slowing redirects.

title: Design an API Rate Limiter
answer: Use a token bucket per API key, with the plan's rate and burst size stored alongside the counter. Run each refill and consume atomically in Redis so requests across API servers share one limit. Return 429 with Retry-After when empty. If Redis is unavailable, apply approximate local limits so the API stays available.
focus: Compare counter and token-bucket designs, then decide how multiple servers share limits.

title: Design a News Feed (Twitter Timeline)
answer: Store each post once, then fan its ID out asynchronously to the recent timelines of active followers. Skip write-time fan-out for accounts with tens of millions of followers and merge their recent posts when a reader opens the feed. Keep timelines as bounded, rebuildable lists of IDs; hydrate and filter posts on the read path.
focus: Choose between write fan-out and read fan-out when a few accounts have millions of followers.

title: Design an Uber-Style Ride-Sharing System
answer: Store each ride request and driver reservation durably, then enqueue matching work through an outbox. Use a spatial cell index to find nearby drivers with fresh location pings, rank a small candidate set by road ETA, and issue expiring offers. Conditional state changes ensure one driver and one ride can be assigned only once, even when replies arrive late or twice.
focus: Design Uber-style dispatch: match nearby drivers quickly without stale locations or double assignments, then isolate a stadium hotspot.

title: Design a Payment System
answer: Create one payment attempt per order and call the provider with a stable idempotency key. Treat a timeout as unknown, then look up the provider's result instead of issuing a new charge. Record signed, duplicate or out-of-order webhooks in an append-only event ledger, apply only valid state transitions, and use an outbox for fulfillment and receipts.
focus: Make retries safe when a payment succeeds but the caller never receives the response.

title: Design a Distributed Job Queue
answer: Put a durable Kafka log in front of the existing Redis worker queues. A relay retries delivery until Redis accepts each job, while workers lease jobs and acknowledge only after success, so a crash can repeat work but cannot lose it. Separate queues by job type, throttle each against its dependencies, and drain backlogs at a rate downstream systems can handle.
focus: Handle duplicate delivery, worker crashes, retries and messages that can never succeed.

title: Design a Video Processing Pipeline
answer: Let browsers upload video directly to object storage with resumable multipart uploads. A durable job record and queue hand each video to a worker under a lease; fencing prevents an expired worker from publishing stale output. Verify every rendition, then atomically mark the video ready. Retries may repeat work, but they cannot expose partial or duplicate results.
focus: Separate upload, durable job state and transcoding so each can recover from failures independently.

title: Design a Dropbox-Style File Sync Service
answer: Split files into verified immutable blocks and publish each version through a conditional metadata manifest. Devices resume uploads by sending only missing blocks, then catch up from a durable per-account change journal. Keep concurrent offline edits as separate versions when they cannot be merged, and check current permissions whenever a device reads shared content.
focus: Keep large uploads resumable and file versions complete while devices reconnect, conflict, lose access and restore deleted data.

title: Design a Product Analytics System
answer: A capture API validates batches and appends events with stable IDs to a durable, partitioned stream. Workers resolve identities and insert large batches into a column store ordered for team and time-range queries. Keep rare properties in JSON, promote frequently filtered properties to typed columns, and deduplicate retries by stream partition and offset.
focus: Keep ingestion durable and deduplicated while making time-range analytics fast for each customer.

title: Design a Notification System
answer: Write product events to an outbox, then let a planner create one deduplicated delivery per user and channel. Put critical, transactional and bulk work on separate queues, and apply preferences again just before sending so unsubscribes take effect. Provider outages delay queued notifications without blocking the product action that caused them.
focus: Prevent duplicate sends, honor preference changes and protect urgent messages when a provider slows down.

title: Design a Distributed Cache (Memcache)
answer: Use a look-aside cache in front of the database and delete cache entries after writes. Give one reader a short-lived lease to refill a missing key, which prevents concurrent misses from stampeding the database and stops an older read from restoring stale data after a delete. Rehash around failed cache nodes and propagate invalidations across clusters.
focus: Control stale reads and database load during writes, hot-key bursts and cache failures.

title: Design Discord's Message Storage
answer: Partition messages by channel and ten-day time bucket, then sort each partition by a time-ordered message ID. Recent-page reads stay small, while old-message lookups can target the right bucket. Keep tombstones short-lived, repair partial rows, and use verified dual writes to move the dataset while it stays online.
focus: Make channel history cheap to read while keeping hot channels and database migrations manageable.

title: Design a Collaborative Editor (Google Docs)
answer: Route every document to one owner that sequences edits and appends them to a durable operation log before acknowledging them. Clients apply local edits immediately, then reconcile concurrent operations with a defined OT or CRDT algorithm; reconnecting clients replay missing operations by sequence. Keep cursors and presence as short-lived state outside the durable edit log.
focus: Preserve one document history through concurrent edits, reconnects, owner changes and fan-out.

title: Design a Reactive Database (Live Queries)
answer: Run each query against a versioned snapshot and record the index ranges it reads. After a commit, compare its writes with those read sets and rerun only affected subscriptions; tag results with one timestamp so a screen never mixes database moments. Validate mutations against the same read sets to preserve rules under concurrent writes.
focus: Update subscribed query results without polling or showing data from mixed snapshots.

title: Shard a Live Postgres Database
answer: Postgres sharding splits data across independent hosts, so writes and table growth no longer land on one primary. Here, shard by workspace so common reads and joins stay together, then map 480 logical shards to hosts. Log writes, backfill versioned rows, compare the copies, and cut over after verification. Replicas and table partitioning solve different limits.
focus: Scale write volume without rehashing every row, and migrate live data without losing newer writes.
